questions.question:
Corregí el ranking como dijiste. Este es el prompt (en inglés) que usaré para generar la especificación:

---
Add the ability for sellers to pause a listing and resume it later without losing its ranking, in the existing marketplace listings API, via `POST /listings/:id/pause` and `POST /listings/:id/resume`.

Why: sellers sometimes need to temporarily take a listing off the market (e.g. out of stock, away) without deleting it and starting over with zero rank.

Behavior:
- A paused listing has status `paused`; resuming sets it back to `active`. Both endpoints return the listing.
- Ranking: the listing's rank score is preserved exactly across pause and resume. Its previous search position is NOT guaranteed after resume — other listings may have advanced meanwhile.
- Who: only the seller who owns the listing, or any admin, may pause/resume. No identified user → 401; a buyer or a seller who is not the owner → 403; unknown listing → 404 (follows the API's current conventions).
- Repeated actions: pausing an already paused listing, or resuming an already active one, succeeds and changes nothing (idempotent).
- Search (`GET /listings`): paused listings are hidden from everyone.
- Direct lookup (`GET /listings/:id`): a paused listing stays publicly visible, showing status `paused`.
- Orders: a buyer cannot order a paused listing — the request is refused with an error and the rank score does not change. The exact error status/code is left to the implementation to choose consistently with the API's conventions; it must be documented.
- Existing open orders on a listing are not affected by pausing it.

Non-goals (v1): time limits or automatic resume (a listing stays paused until manually resumed); recording or exposing when a listing was paused; a "my listings" endpoint for sellers.

References: none beyond the existing API's conventions.

Open decisions: none.
---

¿Lo apruebas?

# Goal — Pause and resume listings

## Goal condition
`npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` all exit 0, and the test suite contains passing HTTP tests proving AC-1…AC-9 below (in particular: a listing paused via `POST /listings/:id/pause` has status `paused`, is absent from `GET /listings`, refuses orders with 409, and after `POST /listings/:id/resume` has status `active`, reappears in search, and has exactly the same `rankScore` it had before the pause).

## Acceptance criteria
- AC-1 `POST /listings/:id/pause` by the owning seller or by any admin sets the listing's `status` to `paused` and answers 200 with the updated listing.
- AC-2 `POST /listings/:id/resume` by the owning seller or by any admin sets `status` back to `active` and answers 200 with the updated listing.
- AC-3 Pausing and resuming change only `status`: `rankScore`, `createdAt` and every other field are exactly what they were before. The listing's search position after resume is not guaranteed — other listings may have gained rank meanwhile.
- AC-4 A paused listing does not appear in `GET /listings` (with or without `q`). Once resumed, it appears again, ordered by the existing ranking rule.
- AC-5 `GET /listings/:id` returns a paused listing to anyone (no user required), with `status: "paused"`.
- AC-6 `POST /listings/:id/orders` on a paused listing answers 409 `{ "error": "listing_paused" }`, creates no order, and leaves `rankScore` unchanged. Orders that were already open when the listing was paused are left untouched.
- AC-7 Pausing an already-paused listing, or resuming an already-active one, answers 200 with the listing unchanged.
- AC-8 Pause/resume errors: no or unknown user → 401 `unauthenticated`; a buyer, or a seller who does not own the listing → 403 `not_listing_owner`; unknown listing id → 404 `listing_not_found`.
- AC-9 Every existing test still passes unchanged.

## Constraints
- No change to existing endpoints' behavior other than AC-4 (search hides paused) and AC-6 (orders refused on paused).
- Error bodies keep the existing `{ "error": "<snake_case>" }` shape; auth keeps using the `x-user-id` header.
- No new dependencies.

## Out of scope
Scheduled or expiring pauses; pause history/audit; notifications to buyers; bulk pause; any UI.

## References
None beyond the current codebase (`src/listings.ts`, `src/orders.ts`, `src/app.ts`).

# Goal — Pause and resume listings

## Goal condition
`npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` all exit 0, and the test suite contains passing HTTP tests proving AC-1…AC-9 below (in particular: a listing paused via `POST /listings/:id/pause` has status `paused`, is absent from `GET /listings`, refuses new orders with an error response, and after `POST /listings/:id/resume` has status `active`, reappears in search, and has exactly the same `rankScore` it had before the pause).

## Acceptance criteria
- AC-1 `POST /listings/:id/pause` by the owning seller or by any admin sets the listing's `status` to `paused` and answers 200 with the updated listing.
- AC-2 `POST /listings/:id/resume` by the owning seller or by any admin sets `status` back to `active` and answers 200 with the updated listing.
- AC-3 Pausing and resuming change only `status`: `rankScore`, `createdAt` and every other field are exactly what they were before. The listing's search position after resume is not guaranteed — other listings may have gained rank meanwhile.
- AC-4 A paused listing does not appear in `GET /listings` (with or without `q`). Once resumed, it appears again, ordered by the existing ranking rule.
- AC-5 `GET /listings/:id` returns a paused listing to anyone (no user required), with `status: "paused"`.
- AC-6 `POST /listings/:id/orders` on a paused listing is refused with an error response, creates no order, and leaves `rankScore` unchanged. Orders that were already open when the listing was paused are left untouched.
- AC-7 Pausing an already-paused listing, or resuming an already-active one, answers 200 with the listing unchanged.
- AC-8 Pause/resume are refused with an error response when: there is no or an unknown user; the caller is a buyer, or a seller who does not own the listing; the listing id does not exist. In every such case the listing is unchanged.
- AC-9 Every existing test still passes unchanged.

## Constraints
- Every new error response uses the existing `{ "error": "<snake_case>" }` shape; the HTTP status and the error string are the implementer's choice within that style.
- No change to existing endpoints' behavior other than AC-4 (search hides paused) and AC-6 (orders refused on paused).
- Auth keeps using the `x-user-id` header.
- No new dependencies.

## Out of scope
Scheduled or expiring pauses; pause history/audit; notifications to buyers; bulk pause; any UI.

## References
None beyond the current codebase (`src/listings.ts`, `src/orders.ts`, `src/app.ts`).

Algunas decisiones de esta corrida podrían valer para todo el proyecto (para no volver a preguntarlas en futuras corridas):
1) Los admins pueden actuar sobre publicaciones de cualquier vendedor, igual que el dueño.
2) Repetir una acción de cambio de estado que ya está en ese estado responde éxito sin cambios (idempotente), no error.
